text:
Mason Marchment is on his sixth NHL team, the undrafted winger who has made a career out of being useful wherever he lands. In San Jose that means 16:30 a night, six goals and 13 points in 26 games, including a power-play goal against Calgary, and a headline this week said he's finding his game.

The numbers around him are rough. The Sharks get only 42% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, three points worse than without him. Some of that is bad luck: San Jose has scored 4.2 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which usually swings back. His own finishing is right where it should be (six goals on 6.4 expected). He's physical, 31 hits. Evolving-Hockey had him 93rd among forwards in wins above replacement last season, a useful middle-six number. Our range projects 38 to 57 points. On a young team, his job is to make the kids' minutes easier, and his second power-play role helps.
